content: Dr. Beverley Biggs has served as an author of technical documents and a speaker for Mead Johnson Nutritionals. Her research unit has received funding from Sight and Life as well as the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to support studies utilizing stable isotopes to investigate the interactions between vitamin A and iron. Dr. Biggs has disclosed that the University of Melbourne has received funding from the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) and the Australian Research Council (ARC) for research on weekly iron and folic acid supplementation during pregnancy. This research was conducted in collaboration with the Research and Training Center for Community Development (RTCCD), the Key Centre for Women’s Health, and the Murdoch Children’s Research Institute. The guideline in question is scheduled for review in 2016. If new information becomes available at that time, a guideline review group will be convened to assess the evidence and revise the recommendations as necessary. The Department of Nutrition for Health and Development at the WHO headquarters in Geneva, along with its internal partners, will oversee the coordination of the guideline update, adhering to the formal procedures outlined in the WHO handbook for guideline development. The WHO encourages suggestions for additional questions to be evaluated during the guideline review process. Plans for updating the guideline on daily iron and folic acid supplementation in pregnant women are in place, with the aim of addressing maternal anemia and improving functional outcomes, such as reducing the risk of low birth weight. The intervention is considered cost-effective and beneficial, with the advantages outweighing potential harms. However, adherence to the supplementation schedule remains a challenge for implementation. The WHO Steering Committee for Nutrition Guidelines Development includes experts from various departments and clusters, such as chronic diseases, nutrition, ethics, reproductive health, immunization, and emergency response. These experts contribute to the development and review of guidelines, ensuring that they are evidence-based and applicable across diverse settings.
